section: 5. Discussion and Limitations - 5.1 What the results mean, and measurement lessons
focus: Panickssery (LLM Evaluators Recognize and Favor Their Own Generations)
context: Must-have citation for section covering: Scoped summary in three sentences: for one model, entries with 2-12 references whose papers fit one prompt and 19% of papers readable in full, access to the source limits agreement with curator-written text far more than how a strategy reads; the levers that moved coverage were access and a completeness pass, not the intermediate representation; the audit has structural blind spots. Do not generalise beyond this regime (notes.md 'Claims the paper must not make'). Address the reviewers' regime objection honestly: direct reading is expected to do well when the papers fit one prompt; the regime where designs might separate (large sets of relevant papers) could not be compared because of stopped replies; the same measurement did resolve a gain of a few points from reading better on 38 held-out entries, so the near-null differences between designs are not only a matter of measurement resolution (phrase as an observation, not a test). Measurement lessons for evaluating evidence-grounded generation, one clause each, no new numbers: treat stopped replies symmetrically across strategies; fix fact lists before scoring; split coverage by whether the supplied text states the fact; report run-to-run noise beside intervals over entries; match settings unrelated to the representation before blaming it; keep per-paper verdicts, since a claim's best verdict hides over-citation; check that a released pipeline runs with the model it will be used with.
